## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The Companions of al-Rass  (`#the-companions-of-al-rass`)

Cited ayat: 25:38-39, 50:12-14

> **25:38** وَعَادًا وَثَمُودَا۟ وَأَصْحَٰبَ ٱلرَّسِّ وَقُرُونًۢا بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ كَثِيرًا
>
> **25:39** وَكُلًّا ضَرَبْنَا لَهُ ٱلْأَمْثَٰلَ وَكُلًّا تَبَّرْنَا تَتْبِيرًا

> **50:12** كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ وَأَصْحَٰبُ ٱلرَّسِّ وَثَمُودُ
>
> **50:13** وَعَادٌ وَفِرْعَوْنُ وَإِخْوَٰنُ لُوطٍ
>
> **50:14** وَأَصْحَٰبُ ٱلْأَيْكَةِ وَقَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ كُلٌّ كَذَّبَ ٱلرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ وَعِيدِ

### Claims

**c1** (25:38): The Quran names 'Ad, Thamud and the Companions of al-Rass, and many generations between them.

**c2** (25:39): For each of them God gave examples, and each He destroyed with total destruction.

**c3** (50:12): Another passage says that before them the people of Nuh denied the messengers, and so did the Companions of al-Rass and Thamud.

**c4** (50:13-14): The same passage names 'Ad, Fir'awn, the brothers of Lut, the Companions of the Thicket and the people of Tubba'.

**c5** (50:14): The passage says that each of them denied the messengers, so that God's threat came due.

### One-minute summary

The Companions of al-Rass are named in lists of peoples who denied the messengers [c1][c3]. The Quran says that God gave examples for each of them and that each was destroyed [c2][c5].

### Complete story

The Quran names 'Ad, Thamud and the Companions of al-Rass, and many generations between them [c1]. For each of them God gave examples, and each He destroyed with total destruction [c2]. Another passage says that before them the people of Nuh denied the messengers, and so did the Companions of al-Rass and Thamud [c3]. The same passage names 'Ad, Fir'awn, the brothers of Lut, the Companions of the Thicket and the people of Tubba' [c4]. The passage says that each of them denied the messengers, so that God's threat came due [c5].

### Deep study

- The Quran names 'Ad, Thamud and the Companions of al-Rass, and many generations between them (25:38) [c1].
- For each of them God gave examples, and each He destroyed with total destruction (25:39) [c2].
- Another passage says that before them the people of Nuh denied the messengers, and so did the Companions of al-Rass and Thamud (50:12) [c3].
- The same passage names 'Ad, Fir'awn, the brothers of Lut, the Companions of the Thicket and the people of Tubba' (50:13-14) [c4].
- The passage says that each of them denied the messengers, so that God's threat came due (50:14) [c5].

### Kids mode

The Quran names the Companions of al-Rass among peoples who did not believe the messengers [c3]. It says that God gave examples for each of them and that each was destroyed [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The lists place the Companions of al-Rass beside other peoples who denied the messengers [c3][c4][c5]. One reading is that the ayat ask the hearer to learn from the examples God gave for each [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the Companions of al-Rass were, where or when they lived, who their messenger was, or what they did; the Quran says none of this.
- Not established: what al-Rass means is read in more than one way; the ayat give only the word.
- Not established: the draft does not say that the Companions of al-Rass and any other people in the lists are the same.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of al-Rass with a well, a place or a people, and the names of their prophet; none is used here.
